title: Reduce streaming token latency: optimize token loop, flush cadence, and backpressure handling
author: Maya Patel
description: Context: streaming token generation has intermittently high tail latency driven by the token emission loop, suboptimal flush cadence for partial frames, and poorly coordinated backpressure between the scheduler and the streaming layer. This PR reduces p95/p99 streaming token latency by optimizing the token loop, adjusting flush cadence heuristics to prioritize low-latency small responses, and adding bounded backpressure signals into the scheduler so workers can shed load smoothly. Changes: 1) Token loop rewrite in runtime/streaming/streamer.rs to batch flushes at micro-batches level and avoid wake storms by adding a fast-path when message queue is single-token. 2) Introduced adaptive flush cadence based on observed token times and downstream consumer ACKs; default cadence reduced for interactive endpoints and can be configured per-route. 3) Backpressure: exporters now emit a lightweight backpressure hint that the scheduler consumes, enabling immediate throttling of batching sizes for congested workers. 4) KV cache touch optimization to avoid unnecessary cache writes during streaming, reducing blocking on cache locks. 5) Kernel selector tweak to avoid reloading compute kernels when streaming-only small sequences are detected. 6) Added microbench harness and integration test for streaming latency and introduced logging hooks for tracing token emission. Benchmarks: synthetic interactive workload across a 128-token average response shows p50 ~8% improvement, p95 ~18% improvement, p99 ~22% improvement, and median per-token generation latency reduced by ~12%. CI and rollout: validated on canary cluster for 72 hours with no regressions; deployed via progressive rollout with canary weight 10% for first 24h and 100% after automated checks. Why this is safe: changes are localized to the streaming path and guarded by feature flags and per-route config; default behavior is unchanged unless explicit route opts in or global toggle enabled for rollout. How to test: run tests/runtime/streaming_latency_test.py with --interactive and compare p99 before/after; use make bench-streaming to reproduce microbench numbers. Related: addresses ENG-1423 (streaming tail latency), follows up on ENG-1487 (kv-cache contention improvements).
